summaries.summary: The page defines Penicillin as a group of antibiotics derived from Penicillium fungi, specifically mentioning types like penicillin G, V, procaine penicillin, and benzathine penicillin with their respective uses. It notes that Penicillin is a β-lactam antibiotic used for treating bacterial infections caused by susceptible Gram-positive organisms. The basic structure is 6-aminopenicillanic acid, and it can be categorized as natural, synthetic, or semisynthetic. The microorganism P. chrysogenum is mentioned as being used.
key_facts: Penicillin is a group of antibiotics derived from Penicillium fungi.
It is a β-lactam antibiotic used for treating bacterial infections caused by susceptible Gram-positive organisms.
Types include penicillin G (intravenous), penicillin V (oral), procaine penicillin, and benzathine penicillin (intramuscular).
Can be natural, synthetic, or semisynthetic.
visible_text: Penicillin is a group of antibiotics derived from Penicillium fungi, including penicillin G(intravenous use), penicillin V (oral use), procaine penicillin, and benzathine penicillin (intramuscular use).
